title: 5 tips for a clean Excel dashboard
author: Arafat Bin Wahahid
excerpt: Simple rules I follow to make Excel dashboards that are easy to read and have zero formula errors.

content.text: A good dashboard answers one question quickly. These are the rules I use in every workbook I build.
1. Keep inputs on their own sheet
Put every number someone may want to change, like growth rate or quota, on an assumptions sheet. The dashboard only reads from it.
Show the three or four numbers that matter most at the top. Everything else supports them.

items: Use colour only to show good and bad
Name your ranges so formulas are easy to read

content.text: If it needs explaining, simplify it.
